newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian PM backs Moslems' plight in Serb village.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian PM backs Moslems' plight in Serb village.

text.p: Bosnia's prime minister complained on Thursday about international pressure to remove Moslems from a devastated village on Serb territory and said the people should be left to make their own decision.
"Do you know what pressure they (the international community) make on us to move those people out?" Hasan Muratovic asked reporters in Sarajevo. "It is simply unbearable."

At least 100 Moslems entered the hilltop hamlet of Jusici on September 20, a war-shattered ghost town just inside Bosnia's Serb republic and also within a NATO-enforced demilitarised area known as the "zone of separation" (ZOS).
Some of the Moslems violated the zone by bringing in weapons which NATO has since confiscated and destroyed.
Serb authorities are demanding Moslems withdraw from the hamlet and return only after submitting to U.N. procedures for the resettlement of villages in the zone.
International officials, including those representing the U.N. refugee and police agencies and NATO, also want the Moslems to withdraw and apply for permission to occupy Jusici.

Those international authorities reported that Muratovic agreed in private meetings to get the Moslems out of Jusici in exhange for a commitment to "fast-track" the U.N. paperwork necessary to get them back in.
Bosnian government radio on Thursday said Muratovic had denied signing any documents regulating the return of refugees to their homes because it would violate the Dayton agreement.
His public statements have been sympathetic to the Moslems.

Comparing them to a salmon, he told reporters: "Like the fish, they are ready to die in order to return to the place where their seeds are. The international community does not understand that. Whoever has got the heart for it can make them (the Moslems) leave."

A Reuters reporter who visited Jusici on Thursday reported the settlement quiet and calm, with Russian paratroopers of the NATO-led peace force providing general security along with unarmed U.N. police monitors.
